subject: Mitigations for burst-induced evictions & follow-up actions
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@oriondata.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@oriondata.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: sudden errors and evictions this morning - urgent

Hi Hannah / Ben —

We started seeing a spike in 5xx errors and timeouts around 08:30 PDT this morning. Roughly 6-8% of our production requests are returning 503 or timing out; tail latency also jumped (p95->p99). This coincides with a burst of concurrent requests from a scheduled batch on our side but the pattern looks like queue amplification on the Redwood dedicated pool.

I've attached a small sample of logs and a short timeline spreadsheet. Can you confirm whether there's an ongoing eviction wave on your end and whether there's a safe fallback you can route traffic to? Our pages are firing and customers are impacted.

Attachments: eviction-logs.tar.gz (logs), timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet)

We need: immediate mitigation steps, ETA for stabilization, and whether you can enable a temporary routing/fallback while you investigate.

Thanks,
Sam Patel
SRE, Orion Data
ops@oriondata.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@oriondata.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden errors and evictions this morning - urgent

Sam — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We're seeing the same symptom in the telemetry: a short burst of allocation churn that triggered a cascade of evictions and increased queueing at the node level.

Immediate actions we are taking now (within next 15 minutes):
- Enable eviction backoff window for Orion Data reserved pool to reduce rapid re-evictions.
- Temporarily route 20% of Orion traffic to a compatible hosted fallback variant (same model family, slightly lower throughput) to reduce pressure.
- Manually scale up two warm standby nodes in the region to increase headroom while autoscaler completes provisioning.

Request for you: please keep the batch window throttled or staggered if possible for the next 2 hours — that will help us stabilize faster. Ben, Marissa: tagging you for the technical details and to confirm ETA on node warmup. I'll set up a quick call in 30 minutes to align and to capture any evidence for a post-incident writeup.

Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success (Escalations), Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden errors and evictions this morning - urgent

Hi all — quick technical note from infra:

Summary of immediate root cause hypothesis:
- We observed a burst-induced KV cache thrash in Orion's tenant slice causing allocator backpressure.
- The autoscaler lagged because new nodes are provisioned from a warm pool but under high contention the warm pool cold-start can still take 4-6 minutes for full readiness.
- Backpressure caused a wave of evictions which in turn amplified queue residence times and produced the 503s at the tail.

Actions taken (already executing):
- Applied eviction backoff to Orion's slice (reduces eviction frequency).
- Lifted a 2-node warm standby from the regional warm pool (+~30% headroom).
- Enabled a conservative routing policy to offload ~20% traffic to hosted fallback (same model family, quantization profile different).
- Opening an incident ticket: JIRA-INC-7429 (internal only).

Next steps / owner:
- Ben Carter: observe telemetry for next 45m and confirm p99 stabilizes.
- Marissa Cole: prepare evidence package (eviction traces + allocator heap dump) and hand to Hannah for customer delivery.
- Hannah: coordinate commercial/credit conversation and confirm if Orion wants the fallback to stay for 24h.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Thanks — appreciate the quick triage. The temporary fallback routing helped immediately (error rate dropped to ~1%). We're happy to keep fallback for the next 24h while you stabilize.

One ask: given the customer impact window (~40 minutes of elevated errors), our leadership will want to discuss a credit. Can you send a proposed credit offer and timeline for the full incident writeup? We'll share vendor questions and any additional logs we captured.

Attached: draft-credit-offer.pdf (placeholder)

Sam

Sam — following up with a concise closure & next steps after our stabilizing actions yesterday: we confirmed stabilization within ~20 minutes of the routing change; p99 latencies returned to baseline and the eviction rate subsided after the two warm nodes reached readiness.

What we are handing off to you now (evidence package):
- eviction-logs.tar.gz: sampled eviction traces and request IDs.
- timeline.xlsx: minute-by-minute timeline we reconstructed.
- allocator-trace.txt (added to Drive): heap & allocator snapshots captured at event peak. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/s/EV-7429-eviction-evidence

Commercials / credits: Marissa and I drafted a credit proposal and attached a placeholder (draft-credit-offer.pdf). We'll formalize the credit within 48 hours and include it in the final post-incident report.

Planned follow-ups:
- Marissa will send the full evidence package to you by EOD today.
- I will publish a formal incident summary (root cause, chronology, long-term mitigations) within 72 hours.
- Proposed long-term mitigations: adjust autoscaler warm pool sizing thresholds for Orion's tenant slice and add a traffic-shaping recommendation for scheduled batch windows.

Please confirm if the evidence packet and credit approach are sufficient to close this out on your side. If you want an optional technical debrief call, we can schedule one later this week.

Thanks again for quick collaboration — sorry for the impact.

Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success (Escalations), Redwood Inference
